name: OK16 cultural hub
watch: Creative cluster in former factory halls at Kastryčnickaja 16 (bank bought them for US$3M); art director Maria Kalesnikava; venue operated by ArtCorporation. Belgazprombank has since tried to sell the buildings.
why_flagged: Creative cluster in former factory halls at Kastryčnickaja 16 (bank bought them for US$3M); art director Maria Kalesnikava; venue operated by ArtCorporation. Belgazprombank has since tried to sell the buildings.
records_note: The Warsaw relaunch has no website and no named funders; Zerkalo (Aug 2026) says the team is formed and funding is being sought.

name: Russian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale
watch: Artists Savchenkov and Sukhareva and curator Malašauskas quit in Feb 2022 and the pavilion stayed shut; lent to Bolivia in 2024 and to a Thomas Heatherwick project in 2025 (protested by the Ukrainian pavilion's co-curator); 2026 return curated by Anastasia Karneeva prompted the European Commission to threaten the Biennale's EU funding (Mar 2026).
why_flagged: Artists Savchenkov and Sukhareva and curator Malašauskas quit in Feb 2022 and the pavilion stayed shut; lent to Bolivia in 2024 and to a Thomas Heatherwick project in 2025 (protested by the Ukrainian pavilion's co-curator); 2026 return curated by Anastasia Karneeva prompted the European Commission to threaten the Biennale's EU funding (Mar 2026).
records_note: The Russian Pavilion has no own site, reports, accounts, funder list or board; its commissioner is named in press but its funding is unpublished.

name: Grand People's Study House
watch: North Korea's Library Law treats libraries as essential for promoting ideology. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State library and Juche study centre: 100,000 m², 600 rooms, claimed capacity 30 million books. A 1989 broadcast claimed over 10 million visits a year; budget unpublished.
records_note: Its official site, gpsh.edu.kp, does not resolve from outside North Korea, so no records could be checked.

name: Korean Central History Museum
watch: Kim Jong Un's 2014 speech called it a model for history museums. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: About 100,000 relics in 19 halls over 10,500 m². The museum claimed 10 million cumulative visitors by 2015; Kim Il Sung founded it in 1945.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; no official website, report, accounts, donor list or board turned up.

name: Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies (Mansudae Overseas Projects)
watch: The UN listing covers all Mansudae operations and subsidiaries worldwide (Panel of Experts, 2017). Its US and EU listings are separate.
why_flagged: Builds monuments abroad, including the African Renaissance Monument in Dakar. Listed by the UN, US, EU and UK for exporting workers to raise revenue for the DPRK government.
records_note: A sanctioned North Korean overseas construction group; searches found only UN, UK and Australian sanctions listings, no website, report, accounts or board.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2008-06 to 2009-03: President Wade's architect told the embassy Senegal would give North Korea about $30M of land in Dakar to build the African Renaissance Monument. A 2009 cable calls the financing murky and the price $16M. (Cablegate 08DAKAR649, 09DAKAR288)

name: Serralves Foundation
records_note: Serralves posts yearly reports with audited accounts from 1989 to 2020 and names founders, but its directors are not named on the governing bodies page.

name: Jewish Museum and Tolerance Center
watch: Endowment managed via Gazprombank asset management per Kommersant; the museum's partners page is empty. Vekselberg also sits on the Tretyakov board.
why_flagged: Partners page lists VTB Bank, Sberbank, SAFMAR foundation, Severstal and Metalloinvest, with Rosneft as an exhibition partner. Founding donors in 2012 to 2014 included Vekselberg, Abramovich and Blavatnik.
records_note: The museum shows partner logos with no date and posts no annual report, accounts or board list; a news item mentions a board meeting.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2008-09: A US embassy cable says Roman Abramovich and Lev Leviev financed the museum, and reports Putin's personal support. Abramovich has been under UK and EU sanctions since 2022; Viktor Vekselberg, also listed as a funder, under US sanctions since 2018. (Cablegate 08MOSCOW2700)

name: Multimedia Art Museum, Moscow (MAMM)
watch: Alfa-Bank is on the US (Apr 2022), UK (Mar 2022) and EU (Feb 2023) sanctions lists. Nornickel itself is not blocked.
why_flagged: Founded by the Moscow Government in 1996, director Olga Sviblova. Partners page lists Nornickel as corporate trustee, Alfa-Bank as strategic partner, plus Live Sound and Priorov Center.
records_note: The museum posts 2025 results and financial reports and plans, names Nornickel and Alfa-Bank as partners without a date, and lists no board.

name: Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts
watch: Marina Loshak left in March 2023; Ekaterina Pronicheva is director now. The board of trustees includes Sberbank, Gazprombank, PSB and Transneft.
why_flagged: VTB is general sponsor of the museum, and PSB partnered the Diamond Chariot Buddhist art exhibition. LG and Yandex Eda are also partners.
records_note: The museum posts activity reports and Treasury financial forms for 2012 to 2025, shows four undated sponsor logos, and names its board of trustees.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2009-03: The museum and the Culture Ministry first refused, then allowed, the US envoy for Holocaust issues to see two works claimed by American families. (Cablegate 09MOSCOW774)

name: Ruarts Foundation
watch: Foundation founded 2003; opened its own building 2021; runs street-art grants. Sardarov is not on EU/UK/US lists (OpenSanctions search Oct 2026 returns only an unrelated Amiran Sardarov).
why_flagged: Foundation founded 2003; opened its own building 2021; runs street-art grants. Sardarov is not on EU/UK/US lists (OpenSanctions search Oct 2026 returns only an unrelated Amiran Sardarov).
records_note: The foundation posts no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; its About page names founder Marianna Sardarova and art director Catherine Borissoff.

name: Winzavod Centre for Contemporary Art
watch: Roman Trotsenko is on the EU list (June 2024) and the UK list (Feb 2025). His son Gleb is on the US list.
why_flagged: Private centre founded in 2007 by Roman and Sofia Trotsenko. Their Winzavod Foundation, led by Sofia, funds its programmes; they put their 2021 artist support at 15-20 million roubles.
records_note: Winzavod posts no annual report, accounts or board; its documents page holds policies and safety assessments, and partners show as logos with no date.

name: Zotov Centre for Constructivism
watch: First Russian institution devoted to constructivism; VTB reports its first-year results on its own culture site.
why_flagged: First Russian institution devoted to constructivism; VTB reports its first-year results on its own culture site.
records_note: It names patrons and partners, VTB as general partner, but posts no annual report, accounts or board; the legal page holds only registrations.
